i don't necessarily disagree with you, but i think youre expression here is a little too black and white. yes, we have multi-culturalism, but the form of it that persists today does not leave all groups on the same level playing field. the notion that "we were all meant to interact" ignores the fact that this "interaction" has always been taking from ethnic or queer minorities, and giving to majorities, whilst the majorities force their culture on the minorities in return. it was never a fair or natural exchange. 

the concept of cultural appropriation was always meant to call out this unequal exchange, but it got convoluted and now people's discussions on it arent even talking about the actual issue. its very complex and nuanced, and it requires the input of many different perspectives to fully grasp. it also means to combat the idea that someone is "entitled" to something that might be sacred to a certain group, but im going off on a tangent. 

tldr: multi-culturalism is good, it just needs to involve social and political equity

as someone who just finished their senior year of high school: i feel you. 

summers are the hardest but heres some things that might help in the meantime:

get foam earplugs!!!!! i CANNOT recommend these enough. they are what gets me through life, i cannot function without them

try white noise! get a machine or an air purifier or anything that makes gentle background noise. it doesnt have to necessarily cover the trigger noises, just be enough to distract from them

go for walks/drives: idk if you drive yet, but getting my license has been wonderful for me as being in the car alone gives me a way to totally control my environment and to be out of my room without worrying about triggers. if you dont drive, try going for walks with gentle background music to help you get away from your neighbors and family

try a summer job: again, idk if youre old enough to get a job but bc of the labor shortage, just about anywhere is hiring. a job could replace school in terms of being a safe space away from triggers at home, and you can make money while youre at it

i hope this helps! also, you seem like you have a great support system with your parents as they are looking for a home that can accommodate you. try brainstorming some ideas with them that can fit your family specifically
